title: Regular Expression Matching
prompt: Given an input string `s` and a pattern `p`, implement regular expression matching that supports `.` and `*` with the following semantics: `.` matches any single character, and `*` matches zero or more of the preceding element. The matching must cover the entire input string, not just part of it.

examples.explanation: "a" alone does not match the entire string "aa".
'*' means zero or more of the preceding element 'a', so "a*" can match "aa".
".*" means zero or more of any character, which covers "ab".

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only
p consists of lowercase English letters, '.', and '*'
It is guaranteed for each appearance of the character '*', there will be a previous valid character to match
hints: Think recursively: does the pattern match the string starting at some position i in s and j in p? Break it down by looking at what p[j] and p[j+1] are.

Define dp[i][j] = true if s[i:] matches p[j:]. If p[j+1] is '*', you have two choices: skip the 'x*' entirely (zero occurrences), or, if s[i] matches p[j], consume one character of s and stay at the same pattern position (one or more occurrences).

If p[j+1] is not '*', it's a simple one-to-one check: s[i] must match p[j] (accounting for '.'), and then recurse on i+1, j+1. Build the table from the end of both strings backward, or memoize the recursion.

solution.approach: Define dp[i][j] as true if s[i:] fully matches p[j:]. Build the table from the back: dp[len(s)][len(p)] = True (empty matches empty). Work backward through i and j. When p[j] is followed by '*', two options exist: treat 'char*' as matching zero occurrences (dp[i][j] = dp[i][j+2]), or, if s[i] matches p[j] (either equal or p[j] is '.'), consume one character of s while keeping the same pattern position, since '*' can repeat (dp[i][j] = dp[i+1][j]). Either possibility being true makes dp[i][j] true. Without a following '*', it's a direct character match: dp[i][j] is true only if s[i] matches p[j] AND dp[i+1][j+1] is true. This correctly handles that '*' operates on the single preceding pattern token and can absorb any number of matching characters greedily or not at all.
